greenwood_craftsman_whole_house_build.heading: Modern Craftsman Whole House Build in Greenwood
greenwood_craftsman_whole_house_build.text1: This Greenwood property was completed in two major phases. Silver Peak built an 850-square-foot rear addition in 2008, then took the structurally compromised 100-year-old primary house down to its foundation in 2018 and rebuilt it as a new, approximately 3,000-square-foot modern Craftsman home with Scandinavian influence.
greenwood_craftsman_whole_house_build.text2: The completed home includes solar panels, an EV charger, an open kitchen, dining and living area, a basement ADU, a primary suite, multiple bathrooms, custom storage, a distinctive shed, and landscaped outdoor spaces.
greenwood_craftsman_whole_house_build.short1: **Project**Modern Craftsman Whole House Build in Greenwood
greenwood_craftsman_whole_house_build.text3: Explore the major exterior, interior, ADU, custom-detail, and outdoor-living decisions that shaped the finished property.

part1.small_heading: Modern craftsman exterior with efficient upgrades
part1.text2: The home was reimagined with a modern craftsman look that kept a familiar Seattle neighborhood character while giving the property a cleaner and more updated presence. Bold exterior color, crisp trim, and a balanced front elevation help create the curb appeal.
part1.text3: Solar panels, an EV charger, custom landscaping, and a distinctive front-yard shed with a living roof make the exterior feel intentionally designed rather than simply refreshed.

part2.small_heading: Custom kitchen details built for everyday use
part2.text2: The kitchen includes a concealed breakfast bar cabinet, quartz work surfaces, under-cabinet outlets, LED lighting, custom Barcelona tile, and quartz window sills. These details keep the room clean visually while making the kitchen more useful day to day.
part2.text3: The backsplash was treated as a design feature, with outlets hidden below the cabinets so the tile can read as one continuous finish.

part3.small_heading: Open kitchen, dining, and living area
part3.text2: The main level was designed around one connected kitchen, dining, and living space. The kitchen acts as the center of the home, while the dining and living areas remain visually connected to patio access, natural light, and the yard.
part3.text3: This layout makes the home feel larger, brighter, and better suited for entertaining, family life, and everyday movement through the main floor.

part4.small_heading: Walnut floors and a custom family room bar
part4.text2: Real walnut floors add warmth and character through the interior. At the back of the home, the family room includes a custom bar designed as a built-in feature rather than a standard cabinet installation.
part4.text3: The bar uses butcher block, open shelving, and metal supports that coordinate with the faucet finish, giving the room a crafted and personal detail.

part5.small_heading: Basement ADU with flexible living space
part5.text2: The lower level includes a basement ADU with its own living area, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, and laundry function. It adds a separate living environment within the property rather than feeling like leftover basement space.
part5.text3: One distinctive feature is the stained original concrete floor with a clear finish, preserving part of the home’s older structure while giving the ADU a unique finish.

part6.small_heading: Primary suite, bathroom, and built-in storage
part6.text2: The primary suite was designed to feel grand and complete, with high ceilings, a walnut beam, layered lighting, and a connected bathroom and walk-in closet. The bathroom includes a long shower layout, bench, double vanity, and two shower heads.
part6.text3: Deep recessed medicine cabinets, interior lighting, outlets, shoe storage, and tailored closet zones show how the private spaces were planned with the same care as the public rooms.

part7.text2: Bathroom and bedroom spaces were treated as part of the full-home scope. Custom tile, updated fixtures, storage planning, and clean finish work help the private rooms feel consistent with the rest of the renovation.
part7.text3: The bathrooms show the level of detail that can go into smaller rooms, where tile, glass, fixtures, cabinetry, and transitions all need to be carefully coordinated.

part8.text2: The backyard was treated as another major part of the renovation. The outdoor space includes a stamped concrete patio designed to resemble cobblestone, basalt stone retaining walls, and an integrated stone bench built into the wall.
part8.text3: A bamboo garden with integrated lighting adds privacy, texture, and atmosphere, helping the yard feel like an extension of the renovated home.

greenwood_craftsman_whole_house_build.text4: Exterior rebuilding and refinishing, open-concept planning, a new custom kitchen, family room improvements, private rooms, bathrooms, and storage.
greenwood_craftsman_whole_house_build.text5: Breakfast bar cabinet, hidden outlets, LED lighting, Barcelona tile, quartz window sills, walnut floors, custom bar, and recessed medicine cabinets.
greenwood_craftsman_whole_house_build.text6: Basement ADU with living area, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, laundry function, and stained original concrete flooring.
greenwood_craftsman_whole_house_build.text7: Stamped concrete patio, basalt stone walls, integrated bench, bamboo garden, landscape lighting, solar panels, EV charger, and living-roof shed.
